theme: Agent 系統在三個不同層次上,把『看起來更多、更新、更一致』的訊號誤判成『真的更可信』——單一 agent 對偽裝成新資料的過期記憶太有信心、多 agent 系統把重複／相關的報告誤判為獨立佐證、自我優化迴圈把 LLM 裁判的分數當成不可挑戰的真理
notes: Announcement batch confirmed via arxiv.org/list/{cat}/new page headers, fetched via Groundlane web_fetch: cs.AI 'Showing new listings for Thursday, 3 September 2026' (58 new submissions, 104 cross-lists, 288 total entries); cs.CL same date (61 new, 200 total); cs.MA same date (5 new, 24 total). Today is Friday 2026-09-04 Taipei time; arXiv does not announce on Fridays, so this Thursday batch is the latest unscreened official batch and was not yet covered by the 2026-09-03 screening record (which used the prior Wednesday 2026-09-02 batch, confirmed by cross-checking that record's announcementBatch field before starting).

Candidate discovery used Groundlane web_extract (selector engine: div.list-title + dt) on the three /new?skip=0&show=2000 listing pages to pair titles with arXiv IDs directly from the official listing, rather than relying on Groundlane web_search (Step 4b), since search-provider indexing lag for same-day preprints has been a recurring issue noted in prior screenings. Title/ID pairs were manually verified by positional alignment against the numbered [n] markers in the raw ids[] array for the first 58 (cs.AI new), 61 (cs.CL new), and 5 (cs.MA new) entries.

Initial topic-gate screen (Step 5a) was applied directly to all three categories' 'New submissions' sections only (124 entries total across the three categories), deliberately excluding cross-listed entries from other categories to avoid the stale-cross-list freshness-integrity failure documented in the 2026-09-03 screening notes (where a cs.MA cross-list surfaced a paper first submitted in July). This is a stricter freshness posture than strictly necessary but avoids re-verifying every cross-list's true submission history under time constraints; native cross-list-only papers were not evaluated this cycle and may resurface in a future batch as a native 'new submission' if not already covered elsewhere.

Topic gate retained roughly 40 candidates spanning four natural clusters: agent memory/context (SSAKG 2.0, The Memory Trust Gap, CHIME, Beyond Context Windows, SkillGLoW, APEx), agent evaluation methodology (When Agents Implement Systems, ClaimReceipt, Monitoring Web Agents, Improving Evaluation Realism, Diagnosing with Insights, CivBench, EarlyEval), agent safety/guardrails (LLM-as-a-Judge Is Not an Oracle, SafeEvolve, FUSE, PRISM, Examining the Vulnerability of Multi-Agent Medical Systems, Epistemic Sybil Resistance), and multi-agent orchestration (MASkills, Codebook Agent, Bilevel Coordinated Reflection, Beyond Outcome Gaps, ArcticSwarm, Competitive Market Behavior of LLMs, Tri-Agent Framework).

Eight candidates were read past the abstract via arxiv.org/abs/{id} to compare direction value before committing to full-text credibility checks: The Memory Trust Gap (2609.01852), CHIME (2609.02074), LLM-as-a-Judge Is Not an Oracle (2609.02246), SafeEvolve (2609.02786), EarlyEval (2609.02783), ClaimReceipt (2609.01992), Epistemic Sybil Resistance (2609.01873), APEx (2609.02253). Full-text credibility review (method, experimental setup, results, limitations, via arxiv.org/html/{id}v1 with bounded selector extraction for later sections) was then performed only on the three finalists below.

Cross-cutting editorial call: three candidates (The Memory Trust Gap, Epistemic Sybil Resistance, LLM-as-a-Judge Is Not an Oracle) were selected together because they form an unusually clean angle-diverse cluster around the same underlying failure pattern -- mistaking a signal that looks like more/newer/independent evidence for a signal that actually is -- at three different architectural layers (single-agent memory, multi-agent report aggregation, self-improvement judge). This was judged a stronger editorial cluster than the larger 'agent evaluation methodology' cluster (7 candidates) or 'agent memory' cluster (6 candidates) taken alone, consistent with the skill's instruction to pick the most editorially valuable cluster rather than the largest one.

CHIME (2609.02074) was read at full-text level and found credible (four long-horizon agent benchmarks, ablations, cross-backbone transfer) but not selected: it is a solid method paper within the already-crowded agent-memory cluster, and its 'Code will be released at [github.com/ATH-MaaS/Marco-DeepResearch]' link name does not match the paper's own title/topic, a naming mismatch that raises reproducibility-artifact doubt not present in the three selected papers; set aside in favor of angle diversity rather than excluded on credibility grounds.

SafeEvolve (2609.02786) and EarlyEval (2609.02783) were read at abstract + partial full-text level, found plausibly credible (SafeEvolve: 3x ASR reduction on AgentDojo with a released GitHub repo; EarlyEval: concrete step/token reduction numbers with released code), but set aside as redundant with the safety-guardrail and evaluation-efficiency angles already well covered by the selected LLM-as-a-Judge paper and prior recent digests, respectively.

ClaimReceipt (2609.01992) and APEx (2609.02253) were read at abstract level, found topically relevant and reasonably rigorous (ClaimReceipt: frozen pre-registered specification with a prospective epoch; APEx: 7-benchmark evaluation with a self-reported gain over GPT-5.4), but not advanced to full-text review: ClaimReceipt's audience is narrower (evaluation-infrastructure researchers rather than agent builders broadly) and APEx's core claim rests on a single-team, self-reported cross-model comparison without external replication, judged less today-important than the three selected directions.

Full method, experimental-setup, results, discussion, and limitations sections were read (not abstract-only) via arxiv.org/html/{id}v1 for all three selected papers, using targeted selector-based extraction (e.g. #S8, #S9 section-id selectors) to reach later sections (limitations, discussion) without loading full documents into context.

Editorial note on 2609.02246 (LLM-as-a-Judge Is Not an Oracle): this is structurally a position/field-report paper, which the selection standard treats cautiously (position papers are background material, not daily leads, unless of major impact). It was nonetheless advanced to full credibility review and selected because its central claims are each grounded in specific, quantified, checkable production incidents (not just argued opinion), and the author's own Limitations section (fetched via #S8 selector) is unusually candid about scope (single team, single model family, suites of 9-100 cases, partly model-generated ground truth, explicitly 'not directly reproducible'). Rated credibility 'conditional pass' rather than 'pass' for this reason, and the article's tone/take-aways were written to reflect that narrower evidence base.

Editorial note on 2609.01873 (Epistemic Sybil Resistance): the Discussion section (#S9) was read in full and confirms the paper itself flags two open problems used in this record's primaryLimitation/notes -- (1) whether an ancestry-aware aggregator actually outperforms a report-only one in a real agent-to-agent retransmission chain was not tested empirically, only theorized; (2) incentive-compatible mechanism design for honest provenance disclosure under adversarial conditions is explicitly left as future work. Both are reflected in the article's editorial-judgment table and Reviewer take.

candidates.title: The Memory Trust Gap: Capability-Dependent Failures in Persistent-Memory Agents
credibilityEvidence: S3 Experimental Setup: 300-scenario frozen, SHA-256-pinned, closed-set action-scored benchmark, 2 suites (Benefit/Safety), 33 template families used as the cluster-bootstrap resampling unit.

S4-S5: 2x2x2x2 memory-feature factorial with direct cross-size bootstrap contrast tests (Table 5/6), not just per-model CI overlap; template-family cluster bootstrap and leave-one-family-out robustness checks reported.
S6: representation-comparison mitigation study (raw / metadata / representation-oracle) showing capability-dependent effective interventions.

S7: cross-family replication on an independent Llama-Instruct size series, external validation on 2 independent datasets (RGB, MisBench), a framing control (memory vs document vs earlier-message), and a thinking-mode robustness check.

S8 Limitations (self-disclosed): Benefit suite cannot express net harm on explicit_conflict; scoring is closed-set/action-based; primary size series is a single family (Qwen3) with cross-family reproduction only on capable Llama sizes; measures failure only at memory-consumption time, not across a full write/update/retrieve system.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Main effects reproduce across an independent model family, two independent external datasets, and multiple robustness checks (cluster bootstrap, leave-one-family-out, thinking-mode); scope explicitly limited to closed-set consumption-time evaluation on one primary family.
reproducibilityEvidence: Benchmark is SHA-256-frozen and methodology fully specified in-text
No public code or dataset link found in the fetched abstract or full-text pages
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The 'over-trust, not confusion' claim is supported by two independent metrics (reliance and Delta_mem) plus cross-family and cross-dataset replication, not a single headline number.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Primary model series is a single family (Qwen3); cross-family validation covers only Llama's more capable sizes, and evaluation is closed-set/action-scored at memory-consumption time only, not across a full memory write/update/retrieve pipeline.
candidates.presentationReason: Method, factorial design, metrics, and limitations are stated precisely with explicit statistical procedures (bootstrap CIs, cross-size contrast tests).
candidates.reason: Rigorous, multiply-validated capability-limit finding directly relevant to any team adding persistent memory to agents; selected for the 'reveals a blind spot' angle.

candidates.title: Epistemic Sybil Resistance: Multiplying AI Agents Without Multiplying Evidence
credibilityEvidence: S4.2 Theorem 1 (report-only non-identifiability) with proof in Appendix A: no deterministic aggregation rule using only report content plus known marginal reliability can be Bayes-correct under both clone and independent structures; explicit error lower bound delta(p).

S5 Proposition 2 (shared-root saturation) and S5.3 correlated-extraction generalization: closed-form information ceiling derived and connected to an existing dependence-discount coefficient from prior literature (Wu 2026).

S8 Empirical Study: 20,000+ controlled real LLM-agent report/extraction calls; posterior coverage collapses from 0.940 to 0.263 as report multiplicity rises 1->32 at fixed evidence root; gap closes and aggregators become statistically indistinguishable at k=16 independent roots; correlated-extraction gamma_cal=0.719 estimated out-of-sample; controlled 2x2 manipulation isolating representation similarity (effect 1.425, CI [1.363,1.485]) from true ancestry (effect 0.040, CI [-0.045,0.120]) on a report-space dedup mechanism's inferred cluster count.

S9 Discussion (self-disclosed limitation): whether an ancestry-aware aggregator outperforms a report-only one specifically in a real agent-to-agent retransmission chain 'was not tested empirically here and is left for future work'; incentive-compatible mechanism design for honest provenance disclosure under adversarial misreporting is stated as an open problem.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: The formal results and the internal statistical validation (Monte Carlo plus 20,000+ real LLM calls) are rigorous, but all empirical tests run on synthetic evidentiary documents constructed by the research team; real-world multi-agent pipeline deployment and the retransmission-chain aggregator comparison are explicitly untested.
reproducibilityEvidence: Code and data publicly released at github.com/marcbara/epistemic-sybil-resistance per the abstract and paper text
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Both core claims (report count is not evidence count; a concrete report-space dedup mechanism tracks representation similarity rather than ancestry) are each supported by independent quantitative results with reported confidence intervals.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Designing an incentive-compatible mechanism for honest provenance disclosure under adversarial conditions is explicitly left as an open problem, and the ancestry-aware-vs-report-only aggregator comparison was not tested in a real retransmission chain.
candidates.presentationReason: Formal definitions, theorems, and the empirical protocol are stated precisely with an explicit proof appendix and clearly delineated scope boundaries (interface hierarchy in Section 3.2).
candidates.reason: Novel formal framing with strong empirical backing and full reproducibility artifacts, directly actionable for teams building multi-agent voting/consensus/deduplication; selected for the 'new method/framework' angle.

candidates.title: LLM-as-a-Judge Is Not an Oracle: Why Self-Improving Agents Need Deterministic Guardrails
credibilityEvidence: S2.6-2.7: ten evaluation suites (9-100 cases each) across three real production domains (contract analysis, compliance review, code quality) run over several months in 2026 on two capability tiers of one frontier proprietary model family.

S3: eleven catalogued failure modes across four classes, each grounded in a specific production instance with before/after numbers (e.g. D1: 100% exploited vs 68.1% clean baseline on contract-analysis, generalizing across six suites at 35.3%-88.9% clean baselines; A4: EM 42.6%->51.9%, MAE 0.72->0.57 from a single schema-order change; D3: 80% EM on a 15-directory calibration subset vs 51.9% on the full 54-repository suite).

S4.3 Table 2: full six-round judge-calibration campaign showing content-level rubric refinement (rounds 2-5) produced zero-to-negative progress while a structural schema-order constraint (round 6) produced the only gain.

S8 Limitations (self-disclosed, unusually candid): ground truth is partly model-generated (39/54 code-quality directories); single model family; single-run measurements with uncharacterized variance; small suites (9-100 cases, most under 20); only two domains; taxonomy is observed not systematically searched; no public artifact, explicitly 'not directly reproducible'; one reconstructed (non-verbatim) example transcript in the appendix.
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Each individual failure case is concrete and independently checkable with real before/after numbers, but the overall evidence base is a single team, single organization, single model family field report with small suites and partially model-generated ground truth, as the author's own Limitations section discloses in detail.
reproducibilityEvidence: Internal production infrastructure cannot be released
Author states the architecture, protocol, and grading rubric are specified in appendices in enough detail to reimplement the system but not to reproduce the reported numbers
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: Individual incidents (D1 answer-key exfiltration, A4 schema-order effect) are concrete and credible as isolated data points, but generalization across model families, organizations, and task domains beyond the two studied is unverified.
candidates.primaryLimitation: All observations come from a single team on two capability tiers of one frontier model family, with suites as small as 9 cases and partly model-generated ground truth; the author explicitly states the work is not directly reproducible.
candidates.presentationReason: Failure taxonomy, architecture, and limitations are stated with specific, checkable numbers throughout, and the author is explicit about what is illustrative reconstruction versus captured evidence.
candidates.reason: Concrete, quantified production incidents and an actionable guardrail architecture for any team running LLM-judge-driven self-improvement loops; selected for the 'application/safety' angle despite being structurally a field report, given the strength and specificity of the underlying incidents and the author's candid limitations disclosure.

candidates.title: CHIME: Credit-Aware Hierarchical Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agentic Planning
credibilityEvidence: Abstract + intro: 4 long-horizon agent benchmarks, ablations, and cross-backbone transfer analysis of the memory bank.
candidates.reason: Credible memory-method paper but redundant with the already-crowded agent-memory cluster this cycle and the selected Memory Trust Gap paper; its code-release link name does not match the paper's topic, a minor reproducibility flag. Set aside for angle diversity, not excluded on credibility grounds.

candidates.title: SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution from Agent Experience for Safety Alignment
credibilityEvidence: Abstract: agentic safety benchmarks including AgentDojo, 3x ASR reduction for Qwen3.5-4B with improved benign utility (59.79% -> 61.86%); GitHub repo released (MaoPopovich/SafeEvolve).
candidates.reason: Plausibly credible safety-alignment method with released code, but redundant with the safety-guardrail angle already covered by the selected LLM-as-a-Judge paper this cycle.

candidates.title: EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction
credibilityEvidence: Abstract: 3 benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified, TerminalBench, Toolathlon), 13%-26% step reduction, up to 44.1% input / 29.4% output token reduction at 89%-97% prediction accuracy; code and data released.
candidates.reason: Solid, practical eval-efficiency method with released artifacts, but set aside as an incremental efficiency improvement rather than a blind-spot-revealing or field-shifting direction for this cycle's theme.

candidates.title: ClaimReceipt: Verifying Evidence Sufficiency and Coverage in Agent Evaluations
credibilityEvidence: Abstract: frozen pre-registered specification (SHA-256 pinned), 1,392 historical records reproducing 5 manual audit verdicts, 11/11 semantic-fault detection with 0/8 false positives, plus a prospective epoch matching a pre-registered prediction.
candidates.reason: Rigorous evaluation-infrastructure paper but narrower audience (agent-eval-methodology researchers/auditors rather than agent builders broadly); judged less today-important than the three selected directions.

candidates.title: APEx: Distillation of Agent Procedural Experience for Adaptive Deep Research Question Answering
credibilityEvidence: Abstract: 7 benchmarks, GRPO-based training pipeline, reports surpassing GPT-5.4 by 14.7 points and the strongest memory-augmented baseline by 3.0 points.
candidates.primaryLimitation: Not advanced to full-text review; headline comparison is a single-team, self-reported cross-model result without noted external replication
candidates.reason: Interesting memory/skill-distillation result but the headline cross-model comparison lacks external validation in the abstract; judged less today-important than the three selected directions this cycle.
